primitives.name: Offensive Line Multiplier
primitives.verbatim_quote: The offensive-line multiplier is the 2024-2025 fit, and the same file is what next week reads.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{ol}': 'dimensionless multiplicative factor representing offensive line fit'}
primitives.assumptions: The multiplier reflects historical performance consistency across seasons; it is static per season but evolves with new data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When starting tackles do not practice fully, M_{ol} decreases linearly with absence severity.

layer2.mapping: GSI computes M_{ol} as a Bayesian prior over tackle availability, updating based on practice logs and injury reports.
layer2.telemetry: Observed tackle practice participation rates and corresponding skill-player performance differentials.

primitives.name: Skill Player Impact
primitives.verbatim_quote: A starting tackle who is out, or who did not practice, lowers the skill players.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{sp}': 'dimensionless impact score quantifying reduction in skill-player effectiveness due to OL absence'}
primitives.assumptions: Impact is proportional to the degree of tackle absence or reduced practice time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: I_{sp} = 0 when all tackles are practicing; increases monotonically with absence duration.

layer2.mapping: GSE encodes I_{sp} into a transition matrix that modifies expected skill-player outputs during game simulation.
layer2.telemetry: Change in average fantasy points per skill player before/after tackle unavailability.

primitives.name: Game Total Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: The total is the posted number on the game file.
primitives.assumptions: T_{g} is fixed at time of game release and represents market consensus.
primitives.breakdown_regime: T_{g} remains constant unless updated by live scoring or official adjustments.

layer2.mapping: GSI uses T_{g} as a baseline in its conformal prediction framework to derive confidence intervals around prop outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation between predicted and actual game totals over multiple weeks.

reasoning_traces.think:
The signal ledger operates under a dual inference model: first, it evaluates each player's contribution through a composite signal derived from availability and practice status. This signal is then mapped into an offensive-line multiplier (M_{ol}), which acts as a scaling factor for team performance. Skill-player impact (I_{sp}) is computed as a function of tackle availability, reducing effective skill-player output when key blockers are absent. These values are combined with the fixed game total (T_{g}) to produce a posterior probability distribution over player props. The system assumes that practice data correlates strongly with performance, and that team edges can be modeled as additive corrections to baseline expectations. Failure modes include misclassification of practice status, overfitting to past data, and ignoring external factors such as weather or coaching strategy.
